title: Attain the depth-four chain connector floor 4m for every 6 ≤ m ≤ 32 (no new κ)
body:
## Result

Exact shortest unsigned word for the depth-four dirty chain connector, for characteristics 6 to 32. The calls are `z_l += B_l z_{l-1}` for l = 1..4. The source x = z_0 is immutable, z_1, z_2, z_3 and y = z_4 start dirty, and the maps are arbitrary. The word must restore z_1..z_3 and add `c B4 B3 B2 B1 x` to y:

```text
shortest length = 4m   for every 6 <= m <= 32 and every c != 0 (mod m)
```

This answers open question 1 of #4249 in that range. #4249 found that depth four costs more than the per-call floor 4m at m = 2..5 (12, 18, 20, 25 calls). The premium is gone from m = 6 on, through m = 32, for all 486 pairs (m, c). With #4249's values, the depth-four minimum is now known exactly for 2 <= m <= 32.

Claim type: **finite certificate** for each listed (m, c). The 4m floor is #4249's Lemma 1/2 argument, restated in the README. No all-m theorem, no new κ, no supplier admission and no selected-frontier change.

Also in the package:
- Lemma 2 writes the six interval counts in terms of three interleaving sequences (calls l-1 before each call l). The verifier checks it on 2,000 random balanced words. It is used only to state the open question.
- Negative findings from a bounded attempt at an all-m construction. At m = 7 the minimum-block witnesses have 16 blocks and use two mirrored {1,2,3} skeletons, with the calls 4 split over three gaps. That skeleton does not extend uniformly (no full coverage at m = 10 or 11). The other structured families tried either force c = 0 or need a cube root of unity mod m.

Only `research/depth4-chain-connector/` is added, on base `12fa8c5c844be21bfefb38a19503fbd867a11244` (priority revision 7, card `connector-alphabet-change`, scope explicitly changed in TASK.json, as in #4249).

## Evidence and reproduction

From the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/depth4-chain-connector/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -O -W error -B research/depth4-chain-connector/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/depth4-chain-connector
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/depth4-chain-connector --check-source-history
```

Locally (CPython 3.12, macOS arm64) both registered commands print `PASS_DEPTH4_CHAIN_CONNECTOR moduli=27 witnesses=486`, with a generated receipt bound to every package and input SHA-256. Each takes about 0.6 s. `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES` pass. For each witness the verifier checks the length 4m, exactly m copies of each call, the interval conditions, an independent UT5(Z/m) matrix product, and two literal replays with dirty registers and random 2x2 maps over Z/m (972 replays). It also runs six rejection controls. Separately, local mutation tests confirmed that a swapped adjacent pair and a wrong-residue word are both rejected.

`search_witnesses.py M C` (simulated annealing, seeded by (m, c)) is how the witnesses were found. It is not part of the replay, because the verifier checks the words themselves.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

Only 6 <= m <= 32 is covered, one finite certificate per (m, c). The m <= 5 minima are #4249's and are not rechecked here. The exploratory family searches behind the negative findings are local and not packaged. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. Every call carries its complete price. Admission, dispatch, routing of the three intermediates, precision, supplier caller and the outer multiplication theorem are not supplied.

## Open next questions

1. Is the depth-four minimum exactly 4m for every m >= 6? A parametric family of the three interleaving sequences of Lemma 2 would prove it. The recorded failed families show which simple shapes do not work.
2. Does the per-call floor km hold at depth k >= 5 for all large m, and from which m on?
3. Does any concrete recursive caller route through three dirty intermediates with a favorable complete invoice for these 4m calls?

## Related open work

- #4249 is the depth-three chain law, and the source of the model, the floor and the m = 2..5 depth-four minima. This package answers its open question 1 for 6 <= m <= 32. No number overlaps: #4249 has no depth-four value for m >= 6, and its 4m floor is the lower bound used here.
- #4257 classifies depth-three count vectors and unequal-price optima. Same chain family, one level shorter, so no number is shared.
- #4236 and #4231 treat the depth-two (one-source) chain and its 2m floor. These are different depths, with no shared number.

## CI notes

Hosted CI is green on head `2183322b32a5975ecb4a6aec2ec8f43ac08b1aec`: [run 39505260880](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39505260880). `plan` passed in 3m11s and the package `replay` passed in 1m17s. No check failed.
